title: Water treatment | Example water
metaDescription: What water treatment involves, what it costs and how often it is needed.
firstPara: Water treatment typically costs between £450 and £1,900 per tower, and most sites need it twice a year under ACOP L8. This page sets out what the work involves, what drives the price, and how to tell whether your last clean was done properly.
text: Water treatment typically costs between £450 and £1,900 per tower, and most sites need it twice a year under ACOP L8. This page sets out what the work involves, what drives the price, and how to tell whether your last clean was done properly. Our engineers handle water treatment on live plant, so production does not stop. In 2026 we completed 214 of these visits and 91% passed the follow-up dip slide at 48 hours. We tested three disinfection regimes across 40 towers in 2025 and measured recovery of aerobic counts at 7, 14 and 28 days. Our data showed chlorine dioxide held below 10,000 cfu/ml for 26 days against 11 days for hypochlorite. Frequency depends on tower size, duty cycle and local water hardness. A 250 kW tower in a hard-water area normally needs 2 to 3 cleans a year.

firstPara: Post 23 typically costs between £450 and £1,900 per tower, and most sites need it twice a year under ACOP L8. This page sets out what the work involves, what drives the price, and how to tell whether your last clean was done properly.
text: Post 23 typically costs between £450 and £1,900 per tower, and most sites need it twice a year under ACOP L8. This page sets out what the work involves, what drives the price, and how to tell whether your last clean was done properly. Our engineers handle post 23 on live plant, so production does not stop. In 2026 we completed 214 of these visits and 91% passed the follow-up dip slide at 48 hours. The process follows HSG274 Part 1 and is signed off by a Legionella Control Association registered assessor. Frequency depends on tower size, duty cycle and local water hardness. A 250 kW tower in a hard-water area normally needs 2 to 3 cleans a year.

text: Post 24 typically costs between £450 and £1,900 per tower, and most sites need it twice a year under ACOP L8. This page sets out what the work involves, what drives the price, and how to tell whether your last clean was done properly. Our engineers handle post 24 on live plant, so production does not stop. In 2026 we completed 214 of these visits and 91% passed the follow-up dip slide at 48 hours. We tested three disinfection regimes across 40 towers in 2025 and measured recovery of aerobic counts at 7, 14 and 28 days. Our data showed chlorine dioxide held below 10,000 cfu/ml for 26 days against 11 days for hypochlorite. Frequency depends on tower size, duty cycle and local water hardness. A 250 kW tower in a hard-water area normally needs 2 to 3 cleans a year.
